title: Kalunga2016 – SSVEP Exo dataset
description: This dataset comprises steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) recordings from 12 healthy subjects performing a brain-computer interface task using flickering LED stimuli at three frequencies (13, 17, and 21 Hz) presented during wheelchair-based exoskeleton experiments. EEG signals were acquired from 8 occipital and parietal electrodes at 256 Hz sampling rate, with 32 trials per session consisting of 8 trials per stimulus frequency and 8 rest trials. The dataset was designed to evaluate online SSVEP-based BCI performance using Riemannian geometry classification methods for assistive robotics applications.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 12 healthy subjects (aged 20-28 years) using a g.tec MobiLab amplifier with 8 electrodes (Oz, O1, O2, POz, PO3, PO4, PO7, PO8) positioned according to the standard 1005 montage with right mastoid reference. Subjects sat in an electric wheelchair with a 20×30 cm LED panel positioned on the left side displaying three groups of 4 LEDs flickering at 13 Hz, 17 Hz, and 21 Hz. Each trial lasted 6 seconds total with a 2-4 second stimulus window and 3-second inter-trial intervals. Subjects followed auditory cues to focus on target LEDs or a central fixation point for the rest class. Signals were sampled at 256 Hz with 50 Hz line frequency filtering.
